guix.note: Findings specific to Guix System and its tooling, from porting it to the F(x)tec Pro¹x. Seeded 2026-10-28 from this repository's git history (commits up to 018fa97) and TODO.md; entries labelled handover were not re-checked. Hardware lessons go in hardware.json, NixOS translation notes in nixos_to_guix.json.

shepherd_services.title: A compositor started from a Shepherd service needs seatd, not elogind
shepherd_services.general: libseat needs a seat session. A Shepherd service that runs the compositor through 'su -l user' gets no PAM/logind session, so libseat fails with elogind ('Failed to load session backend', 'Failed to start a DRM session') even though elogind runs and /dev/dri exists. seatd-service-type gives libseat a socket that needs no session; the user must be in the seat group. seatd also provides the 'elogind Shepherd symbol, which services such as phosh require for start order.
shepherd_services.instance: phoc/phosh on the Pro¹x, systems/mobile.scm. Later replaced by greetd + tuigreet as session picker, which owns VT1.

shepherd_services.title: A daemon's D-Bus policy is only loaded if the service extends dbus-root-service-type
shepherd_services.general: Installing a package does not install its D-Bus system policy. Unless the Guix service extends dbus-root-service-type with the package, dbus-daemon refuses the daemon's bus name. Some daemons, like ModemManager, then exit with status 0 and no useful message, and Shepherd disables them after repeated restarts.
shepherd_services.instance: ModemManager exited five times at boot and was disabled. Fixed by the extension in fxtec-pro1x/services/modem.scm; NixOS's networking.modemmanager.enable did this implicitly.

shepherd_services.title: Do not give #:pid-file to a daemon that runs in the foreground
shepherd_services.general: make-forkexec-constructor with #:pid-file waits for the file to appear. A daemon started in the foreground never writes it, so Shepherd waits until the timeout and marks the service failed although the daemon runs. Leave #:pid-file out and Shepherd tracks the child it started.

shepherd_services.title: Shepherd requirement means 'start after', and fails if the requirement cannot start
shepherd_services.general: A Shepherd 'requirement' starts the required service first and refuses to start the dependent one if that fails. It is not systemd's Wants=, which tolerates a failed dependency. Translate systemd After=/Wants=/Requires= deliberately, service by service.
shepherd_services.instance: ModemManager requires rmtfs/tqftpserv in modem.scm; behaviour once MM stays up is still to be checked (TODO.md section 6).
shepherd_services.source: TODO.md section 6; confirm in the Shepherd manual and with herd status after the next flash

shepherd_services.title: D-Bus-activated daemons do not appear in herd status
shepherd_services.general: A daemon started by dbus-daemon on first use (NetworkManager here, iio-sensor-proxy on other systems) is not a Shepherd service. 'herd status' does not list it; check with ps, or with busctl or dbus-send on its bus name.
shepherd_services.instance: NetworkManager running and nmcli working on the Pro¹x while absent from herd status.

shepherd_services.title: /etc/environment.d is a systemd convention; check that anything reads it on Guix
shepherd_services.general: systemd's environment.d is read by the systemd user manager, not by PAM. On a Guix system without systemd, a file placed there may be ignored. Use the session start script, a service's #:environment-variables, or /etc/environment (pam_env) instead, and verify the variable inside the running process (/proc/<pid>/environ).
shepherd_services.instance: fxtec-pro1x/services/camera.scm writes LD_LIBRARY_PATH for libcamera-pro1x to /etc/environment.d/51-pro1x-libcamera.conf, with a comment saying PAM reads it. The NixOS port sets it on the wireplumber user service instead. Not checked on the device.
shepherd_services.source: fxtec-pro1x/services/camera.scm lines 37-45 at 018fa97, read in source; confirm with: tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(pgrep -n wireplumber)/environ | grep LD_LIBRARY_PATH

shepherd_services.title: Step the clock at boot with ntpd -g; openntpd did not
shepherd_services.general: A phone without a battery-backed clock at first boot can start in 1970, and TLS, substitutes and guix pull fail until the time is fixed. openntpd-service-type did not step it; ntp-service-type with allow-large-adjustment? #t passes -g, which lets ntpd make one large step.
shepherd_services.instance: systems/mobile.scm and mobile-encrypted.scm. Fix not yet seen on the device as of TODO.md section 7.

shepherd_services.title: An etc-service entry under a directory makes the whole directory a read-only store link
shepherd_services.general: On Guix System, each top-level /etc entry produced by etc-service-type is a symlink into the store. Adding "NetworkManager/conf.d/x.conf" or "dconf/db/local.d/x" makes /etc/NetworkManager or /etc/dconf read-only, so daemons and activation snippets that write there fail (NetworkManager system-connections, dconf update). Use the service field made for it (network-manager-configuration extra-configuration-files), or build the file at build time (dconf compile in a computed-file), instead of writing beside a store link.
shepherd_services.instance: Earlier note (2026-10-26, handover from 491cd95) said /etc is read-only on Guix and moved NM connections to /var/lib; wrong cause: /etc is writable, the nm-unmanaged-usb0 etc entry made /etc/NetworkManager a store link. Activation logged mkdir EROFS for /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections and "Failed to create file /etc/dconf/db/local.BTAPAA: Read-only file system" from pro1x-keyboard (dconf update), at boot and on deploy, so the dconf system db never existed. Fixed: conf.d files via extra-configuration-files (the /var/lib keyfile path kept so saved networks stay), dconf db compiled at build time.
shepherd_services.source: generation 2 activate run by hand on the phone; ls -la /etc/NetworkManager /etc/dconf; gnu/services/networking.scm network-manager-activation (Guix fa73e81)

shepherd_services.title: phoc started outside a desktop session needs its own session bus
shepherd_services.general: GSettings calls block indefinitely when there is no session bus. A compositor started by a system service or a greeter command must be wrapped in dbus-run-session, and needs XDG_DATA_DIRS pointing at the system profile so gschemas.compiled is found.
shepherd_services.instance: phoc -E phosh wrapped in dbus-run-session; stale Wayland sockets removed before restart.

shepherd_services.title: A greeter that owns VT1 means removing mingetty, login and console-font from %base-services
shepherd_services.general: greetd on VT1 conflicts with the mingetty on tty1 from %base-services. Removing the mingetty services also requires removing console-font, which depends on the term-ttyN services that mingetty provides.
shepherd_services.instance: systems/mobile.scm, greetd + tuigreet offering Phosh and Sxmo/Sway sessions from /etc/wayland-sessions.
shepherd_services.source: systems/mobile.scm lines 260-262 at 018fa97, read in source; commit 1226034

shepherd_services.title: A udev-service-type extension must be a directory with lib/udev/rules.d/; a bare rules file is dropped silently
shepherd_services.general: udev-service-type unions the lib/udev/rules.d/ directories of the items it receives (packages or the output of udev-rule / file->udev-rule). A local-file, plain-file or computed-file holding rule text has no such directory and is ignored without any warning; the system builds and boots, and the rules simply are not there. Wrap rule files with file->udev-rule "NN-name.rules" FILE. A service that installs a daemon also has to pass the daemon package itself if its own rules matter (ModemManager, iio-sensor-proxy), as the stock Guix services do.
shepherd_services.instance: services/hardware.scm passed (local-file "60-pro1x.rules") and services/sensors.scm a computed-file "90-pro1x-sensors.rules"; on image 6b37ac4 neither file was in /etc/udev/rules.d, and pro1x-modem-service-type did not pass modem-manager-1.24, so 77-mm-qcom-soc.rules was missing too. Consequences: no rmnet_ipa0 tags (MM: no net port), no haptics/slider/sensor rules. Fixed with file->udev-rule plus the two packages; re-test pending.
shepherd_services.source: phone survey 2026-10-28 (ls /etc/udev/rules.d, udevadm test); /tmp/guix gnu/services/base.scm udev-configurations-union, file->udev-rule

shepherd_services.title: Guix extlinux.conf has no Default entry and multi-word labels
shepherd_services.general: Guix writes extlinux.conf as: header, the current system as entry 1, then older generations newest first, each LABEL being the generation label (with spaces). Scripts that index entries or reuse LABEL as a DEFAULT target must not assume NixOS layout (a leading Default entry) or one-word labels.
shepherd_services.instance: services/boot.scm (from NixOS boot-menu.nix) used entry N+2 and LABEL $2; changed to N+1 and the full label in f737b70. Phone: one generation only, so prev*.conf was never written.
shepherd_services.source: /boot/extlinux/extlinux.conf on image 6b37ac4; gnu/bootloader/extlinux.scm; NixOS modules/boot-menu.nix line 20-23

packaging.title: Installing GSettings schemas: the package must be in the system profile
packaging.general: Guix compiles GSettings schemas per profile. A program whose schemas are not compiled into the profile it runs from crashes at the first g_settings_new() for a missing schema. Put the package providing the schema in the system 'packages' field (not only as a service's dependency), or bundle the schemas.
packaging.instance: phoc crashed at start until phoc-pro1x was added to the system packages for mobi.phosh.phoc.gschema.xml.

packaging.title: Bundle a few schema XMLs instead of pulling a large package for them
packaging.general: When a package only needs a handful of another project's GSettings schemas, ship those XML files with the package and compile them in a phase, instead of adding the whole project as an input. Note the upstream version they came from, and refresh them on upgrades.
packaging.instance: phosh-pro1x needs three org.gnome.settings-daemon schemas; gnome-settings-daemon as an input pulled evolution-data-server and webkitgtk, hours of building on aarch64. Schemas now in device/phosh/.

packaging.title: In a meson build phase, call glib-compile-schemas by name, not via search-input-file
packaging.general: search-input-file on native-inputs did not find glib-compile-schemas from glib:bin inside a custom phase, although the meson build system has it on PATH. Calling the program by name works.
packaging.instance: phosh-pro1x install-missing-schemas phase; three consecutive commits before it built.

packaging.title: Newer phone stacks pull version chains Guix does not have yet
packaging.general: A recent mobile shell can require newer middleware than the distribution ships, which in turn requires newer libraries. Package the whole chain in the channel, disable optional features whose own dependencies fail (introspection, MBIM, plugins), and write each disabled feature down at the package definition.
packaging.instance: phosh 0.56 needs mm-glib >= 1.24, so ModemManager 1.24, which needs libqmi >= 1.36. Introspection disabled in both (g-ir-scanner failure), MBIM disabled. phosh lockscreen plugins disabled (evince dependency); quick-setting plugins re-enabled once qrcodegen-cpp was added. phosh needs gcr-3, not gcr 4.

packaging.title: Replace extlinux-bootloader by a stub when U-Boot reads extlinux.conf itself
packaging.general: Guix's extlinux-bootloader depends on syslinux, a BIOS-era build that fails with GCC 14 (-mregparm=3) and is useless on an arm64 phone. Since U-Boot reads extlinux.conf natively, a custom bootloader with a no-op installer only needs to write the configuration file.

packaging.title: Cross-gcc for U-Boot fails in fixincludes in the non-FHS build sandbox
packaging.general: gcc's stmp-fixinc rule expects /usr/include, which does not exist in the Guix build sandbox. Configure the cross compiler with --disable-fixincludes. The grafted cross toolchain hit the same failure; building U-Boot with --no-grafts used the cached ungrafted one.

packaging.title: Prefer url-fetch tarballs over git-fetch when CI cannot run git
packaging.general: git-fetch origins need a working git in the build environment. On the GitHub runner, Guix's git-minimal exited with status 128 for every fetch. Release or archive tarballs through url-fetch avoid it; the hash then pins the tarball, not the commit.
packaging.instance: libqrtr, qbootctl, tqftpserv, rmtfs, hexagonrpcd, cameractrl switched to url-fetch.

packaging.title: Check for aarch64 substitutes before choosing a large application
packaging.general: Without substitutes, large packages build on aarch64 for hours or run out of memory (LTO links). Check with 'guix weather --system=aarch64-linux <package>' before adding one to the system.
packaging.instance: firefox had no aarch64 substitutes and ran out of memory at the LTO link; icecat had substitutes on ci.guix.gnu.org (about 78 MB).

packaging.title: phoc needs the wlroots it embeds, with phoc's patch; building it against a distribution wlroots breaks the Phosh home bar
packaging.general: phoc ships wlroots as a meson subproject with patches under subprojects/packagefiles/wlroots. Phosh relies on them (0.56: a revert allowing layer surfaces of height 0 without top and bottom anchors). Packaging phoc against the distribution wlroots needs the same patches on a separate wlroots variant; patching phosh around the resulting protocol error instead hides the home bar (surface 15 px, folded by a margin computed for the full height).
packaging.instance: phoc 0.56.0 against Guix wlroots 0.20.2. Phosh debug log: Configured phosh home (540x15), on_configure_event 137x540 margin -122, no bar on screen (screenshots). Fixed in 8897846 with wlroots-for-phoc and without fix-home-bar-height.patch (1b5d016).
packaging.source: phoc-v0.56.0 subprojects/wlroots.wrap and packagefiles; phosh src/home.c get_margin; /tmp/phosh-1000.log with G_MESSAGES_DEBUG

packaging.title: phosh 0.56 needs mutter keybinding schemas, a PAM service named phosh, and lives in libexec
packaging.general: Running phoc+phosh without gnome-session and without mutter: phoc aborts without the org.gnome.mutter.keybindings schema; the lock screen authenticates with PAM service phosh and falls back to other (deny) without it; phosh 0.56 installs the shell in libexec and bin/phosh-session starts gnome-session.
packaging.source: /tmp/phosh-1000.log on the phone; ls of the phosh-pro1x output; /etc/pam.d listing

packaging.title: A channel that uses another channel must declare it in .guix-channel; test pulls with guix time-machine, not -L
packaging.general: guix pull builds a channel with only its declared dependencies on the load path. A channel whose modules import another channel (nonguix here) fails with "no code for module" unless .guix-channel lists it under dependencies. Loading the tree with -L on a host that has the other channel pulled hides this. The reliable test is guix time-machine with a channels file pointing at the local repository (file:// URL, commit), without --disable-authentication. Copy channel introductions from the upstream README or source, never retype them: a wrong commit fails with "Git error: object not found".
packaging.instance: fxtec-pro1x: nonguix introduction had ...d4d796ab instead of ...d4d59fbc (pull on the phone: object not found); the guix introduction in channels-lock.scm and channels-ci.scm was c91e27c6 instead of 9edb3f66; .guix-channel had no dependencies. Fixed in cb401e1; time-machine with guix 8b96d76, nonguix c241d19 and the local commit builds the channel.
packaging.source: author pull log on the phone; GitLab API commit lookup (404 vs 200); /var/log/guix/drvs/gm/5smv8pyx…-fxtec-pro1x.drv.gz; guix/channels.scm %guix-channel-introduction

packaging.title: Guix's iio-sensor-proxy polkit substitution eats a newline in 3.9
packaging.general: A substitute* pattern ending in '.*' consumes the line's newline; it was harmless while the next line was empty. When inheriting a recipe for a newer version, check what its substitutions do to the new source.
packaging.instance: iio-sensor-proxy 3.9 meson.build: 'polkit_gobject_dep\\..*' glued libssc's dependency line onto the policy directory ('meson.build:48:115: ERROR: Expecting eof'). Replaced with an exact pattern.
packaging.source: reproduced with substitute* on the 3.9 source; commit e4051eb

packaging.title: Tests that need a mock QMI server do not run in the build sandbox
packaging.general: Stop after the second environment gap (missing /usr/bin/env, then PyGObject) and disable the tests with the reason, rather than rebuilding a test environment.
packaging.instance: libssc 0.4.4: mock SSC server in Python; nixpkgs does not run the tests either. iio-sensor-proxy 3.9: SSC accel and proximity tests pass, compass and light time out under QEMU (skipped).

packaging.title: gtklock 4.0.0 dies at lock time under Sway: committed surface size does not match the acked configure
packaging.general: A session locker that dies leaves Sway locked with a red screen and nothing to type into. Before switching lockers, run the new one in a throwaway headless Sway (WLR_BACKENDS=headless, short XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for the socket) and grab the screen with grim.
packaging.instance: gtklock 4.0.0 (gtk-session-lock 0.2.0) from the pinned Guix, with and without gtklock-virtkb-module, in headless SwayFX 0.6 and plain Sway, at scale 2 and scale 1: Wayland error on ext_session_lock_surface_v1 'committed surface dimensions do not match last acked configure', Gdk protocol error 71, red lock screen. Not tried on the phone. swaylock-effects works there.
packaging.confidence: confirmed (headless on the PC); inferred for the phone
packaging.source: WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 gtklock log; scratchpad mock-up runs

ci.title: Running guix-daemon on GitHub Actions runners: the obstacles met
ci.general: A hosted Ubuntu runner is a hostile place for guix-daemon. Seen here: systemd PrivateTmp and AppArmor breaking mkdtemp in /tmp, the build-users group missing in unprivileged installs, chroot builds impossible without privileges (--disable-chroot), client/daemon version mismatch after guix pull (restart the daemon), channel authentication and signing keys for nonguix and bordeaux, and disk space for a system image. A self-hosted aarch64 runner or building locally avoids most of it.
ci.instance: .github/workflows/build.yml, channels-ci.scm. 34 commits starting with 'ci:' between 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-28, most of them on 2026-10-25 and 2026-10-26.

ci.title: Reproduce a CI failure locally before pushing another fix
ci.general: Each push-and-wait cycle on hosted CI costs many minutes, and guessing one flag per push produces long chains of fix commits. Reproduce the failing step in a local container or VM, or add the diagnostics first and change the setup only once the cause is known. This is the two-failed-fixes rule of AGENTS.md section 4 applied to CI.
ci.instance: The daemon sandbox flags alone went through --no-sandbox, a systemd drop-in resetting the daemon to root, stripping User=/Group=, then --disable-chroot (commits e227e9d, 19355ca, 9c63efb, 3e6889b).
ci.source: git log of this repository, read 2026-10-28

ci.title: Do not let a pipeline hide the exit status of the build
ci.general: 'guix system image ... | tail -1' returns the status of tail. Use set -o pipefail and capture the output separately, or the CI step passes with no image.

ci.title: With --disable-chroot, guix-daemon builds in its TMPDIR; a small /tmp tmpfs breaks system image builds
ci.general: Without chroot, guix-daemon puts build directories under its own TMPDIR (default /tmp). The partition.img builder of guix system image stages the whole system closure and then writes the ext4 image in that directory, so it needs roughly twice the closure size. A size-limited tmpfs on /tmp lets every package build and fails only at the very end, with the note "build failure may have been caused by lack of free disk space". Give the daemon a TMPDIR on a disk with room (Environment=TMPDIR=... in its unit).
ci.instance: Run 40702633350 (commit 018fa97): /tmp was a 4G tmpfs (added in 9258bcf for mkdtemp), root disk had 120G free; failed in x434...-partition.img.drv. Fixed by TMPDIR=/var/tmp/guix-build. Not yet verified by a green run; the builder log itself was not printed, so the cause is inferred.

deployment.title: Previous generations are the rollback, written as separate extlinux menus
deployment.general: Every reconfigure creates a system generation. With U-Boot reading extlinux.conf, the previous generations must be written somewhere U-Boot offers them, or rollback only works from a running system (guix system roll-back).
deployment.instance: pro1x-boot-menu-service-type (fxtec-pro1x/services/boot.scm) splits extlinux.conf into per-generation files for 3 previous generations; the count must equal the value compiled into U-Boot. Chosen by holding volume-down at power-on.

deployment.title: scripts/update.sh uses NixOS commands that do not exist on Guix
deployment.general: Deployment scripts carried over from a NixOS port need a rewrite, not a translation of names: switch-to-system is NixOS's activation script, and 'guix system reconfigure' takes a configuration file, not a system directory. guix deploy, or reconfigure run on the device, are the Guix ways.
deployment.instance: scripts/update.sh runs 'guix system reconfigure /run/current-system --no-bootloader' then '/run/current-system/bin/switch-to-system' on the phone. --no-bootloader would also keep new generations out of the boot menu. Not run; TODO.md section 10. Replaced on 2026-10-28 by scripts/deploy.sh running guix deploy with deploy/pro1x.scm (root SSH by key); first deploy 2026-10-28 (generation 3, after the ACL fix).
deployment.source: scripts/update.sh lines 30-32 at 018fa97, read in source

deployment.title: guix deploy needs the build host key in the deployed system authorized-keys
deployment.general: guix deploy (authorize? #t) adds the host signing key to the target /etc/guix/acl before copying, but activating the new system rewrites the ACL from guix-configuration authorized-keys. The next copy (bootloader installation) is then refused with "unauthorized public key": the new generation is current but not in the boot menu. Add /etc/guix/signing-key.pub of the host to authorized-keys of the deployed operating-system.
deployment.instance: First deploy 2026-10-28: generation 2 made current, then failed; /etc/guix/acl held only the two substitute keys and extlinux.conf still listed generation 1 only. deploy/pro1x.scm now wraps the system with with-host-signing-key.
deployment.source: deploy log (window local-pc); cat /etc/guix/acl on the phone

deployment.title: Running a system activate script by hand activates the booted system unless GUIX_NEW_SYSTEM is set
deployment.general: activate-current-system takes the system from GUIX_NEW_SYSTEM, else from gnu.system= on the kernel command line. Running <system>/activate by hand without the variable points /run/current-system back at the booted generation.
deployment.instance: Ran generation 2 activate on the phone booted into generation 1; /run/current-system went to generation 1 (pizz8…). Restored with GUIX_NEW_SYSTEM=<gen2> <gen2>/activate.
deployment.source: readlink /run/current-system on the phone before and after

deployment.title: guix deploy records the host guix channels as provenance; override current-channels in the deploy file
deployment.general: machine-operating-system adds provenance from (guix describe) current-channels, i.e. every channel of the guix running guix deploy. To record only the channels the system is meant to follow, module-set! current-channels in (guix describe) from the deploy file; (gnu services) reads the same variable. Separately, guix-configuration channels sets /etc/guix/channels.scm, which guix pull on the target uses.
deployment.instance: deploy/pro1x.scm (dcb2dec) keeps guix and nonguix from the host and adds fxtec-pro1x at git HEAD. Generation 4 on the phone lists exactly these three; generations 2 and 3 listed all of the host channels.
deployment.source: gnu/machine.scm, gnu/services.scm provenance-entry, guix/describe.scm (Guix fa73e81); guix system list-generations on the phone

deployment.title: A deployed generation can activate fine and still not boot: deploy never runs its initrd
deployment.general: guix deploy and reconfigure activate the new system on the running kernel; the initrd, the root mount and the kernel command line are first exercised at the next boot. A file-system entry with (options "noatime") activates without complaint, but the initrd passes it to mount(2) as ext4 data and stops with "unknown parameter" in the Guile REPL. Use (flags (quote (no-atime))). Before rebooting into a deployed generation, keep a known-good one in the boot menu that does not share the change.
deployment.instance: Generations 2-5 (deployed 2026-10-28) all stopped at "ext4: unknown parameter noatime" / mount: invalid argument. Generation 1 (image) booted because the image builder writes its own root entry (root=UUID, no options). The U-Boot previous-generation slots (prev1-3) pointed at 4, 3, 2, so no menu entry reached generation 1. Recovered by U-Boot USB mass storage from the PC: generation 1 moved first in /boot/extlinux/extlinux.conf (original kept as extlinux.conf.bak). Fixed in 3b1c86d.
deployment.source: author report of the boot screen; extlinux.conf and prev*.conf read over UMS; gnu/build/file-systems.scm (Guix fa73e81)

deployment.title: Deploy the phone's own configuration, built on the PC
deployment.general: Deploying a system file from the development tree replaces the owner's configuration. Copy the owner's config.scm and channels.scm from the device, build under guix time-machine with those channels, and put the tree's modules first with -L for unpushed work. Keep the deploy key in root's authorized keys whatever the config says.
deployment.instance: scripts/deploy.sh since 2026-10-30; --repo keeps the old mode. First run built go-std and tailscaled for aarch64 under QEMU.

deployment.title: Do not rewrite a bash script while it runs
deployment.general: bash reads a script from disk as it executes; replacing it during a long command makes bash continue at the old byte offset in the new text. Keep edits aside until the run ends.
deployment.instance: Pro1X: scripts/deploy.sh rewritten while guix deploy ran from it; restored byte for byte before the deploy returned.

deployment.title: Deploys over Tailscale work; check the host key against the USB one
deployment.general: guix deploy to the phone's tailnet address works as over USB. Add the tailnet address's host key only after comparing its fingerprint with the key seen over the cable. Keep the tailnet address out of git (add it to the private patterns).
deployment.instance: Pro1X 2026-10-30: several deploys over the tailnet.

deployment.title: When deploying past unbuilt kernel changes, revert them all in the worktree and compare the kernel path
deployment.general: To deploy userspace fixes while a kernel change waits for CI, deploy from a worktree where every kernel change is reverted (patches and config), and compare the worktree's kernel store path with the phone's (/run/current-system/parameters) before deploying; a missed config line starts a multi-hour kernel build under QEMU.
deployment.instance: Pro1X: a worktree without the new patch but with the new CONFIG_LEDS_TRIGGER_PATTERN started a kernel build; caught and stopped.

deployment.title: git commit <path> leaves new files out
deployment.general: Committing with a path argument skips untracked files under it; a package that refers to such a file builds only from the working tree. Look at the ?? lines of git status before pushing, or build from a clean worktree.
deployment.instance: device/sway/pro1x.conf was never committed (f725625), so main failed to build for others for hours; found by deploying from a worktree.

licensing.title: The NixOS port has no licence file; code taken from it has no stated licence
licensing.general: A repository without a licence grants no reuse rights by default. Before relicensing material from another port under the channel's GPL-3, ask its author to add a licence, and keep its origin stated where it is used.
licensing.instance: nyymi609/fxtec-pro1x-nixos at commit 579356e has no LICENSE or COPYING file and GitHub detects no licence. This channel (GPL-3) carries its kernel patches, UCM2 profiles and scripts under device/.
licensing.source: clone of nyymi609/fxtec-pro1x-nixos at 579356e, root listing; GitHub API license field empty

desktop.title: Without logind, every allow_active polkit action is refused: add the package's actions and a group rule
desktop.general: polkit grants allow_active actions only to the active local session, which it learns from logind. With seatd it never knows, so ModemManager, NetworkManager, iio-sensor-proxy and friends refuse requests from the logged-in user. Two separate faults look the same: the package's actions not given to polkit-service-type ('Action ... is not registered', even as root), and no rule for the user ('Not Authorized'). Give the package to polkit-service-type and add a rule for a group.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: GNOME Settings' SIM unlock closed without error (ModemManager: PolicyKit authorization failed); 'Action org.freedesktop.ModemManager1.Device.Control is not registered' even for root; 'net.hadess.SensorProxy.claim-sensor is not registered', then 'Sensor claim not allowed'. Fixed: modem-manager and iio-sensor-proxy in polkit-service-type, rules for netdev and users.
desktop.source: commits 84d1ca4, b3d83fb, bd2c999, dbf9f11; logs on the phone

desktop.title: A deploy does not reload the system bus or polkitd
desktop.general: After guix deploy or reconfigure, the running dbus-daemon keeps its old policy and polkitd its old actions and rules (it watched the previous /etc/polkit-1 store link): new D-Bus services and polkit actions work only after a reboot. Reload the bus (org.freedesktop.DBus.ReloadConfig) and stop polkitd at activation.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: UPower exited with 'name lost, exiting' until ReloadConfig; polkit kept 'not registered' until polkitd was restarted. pro1x-reload-bus-service in system/common.scm does both when the bus runs.
desktop.source: commit 7d1b585; upowerd -v and polkit errors on the phone

desktop.title: A package that is only a dependency exposes no D-Bus session service
desktop.general: D-Bus-activated daemons (feedbackd, xdg-desktop-portal) start only if their service file is under a directory the session bus reads (XDG_DATA_DIRS: the system or user profile). Being in the store as a dependency of Phosh or Calls is not enough.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: feedbackd 0.8.1 in the store, never started, no vibration; no xdg-desktop-portal, so libadwaita apps ignored dark mode; no UPower, so no battery in Phosh. All added to the system profile or as services.

desktop.title: Phosh without gnome-session: what gnome-session would have started
desktop.general: Phosh leaves some jobs to helpers gnome-session starts: the volume keys to gnome-settings-daemon's gsd-media-keys (it grabs them through Phosh), dimming to gsd-power (which needs logind). Start what works without logind from the session wrapper, replace the rest.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: volume keys did nothing until gsd-media-keys ran (author confirmed); its logind and session-manager warnings are harmless. Dimming done with swayidle + pro1x-dim instead of gsd-power.

desktop.title: Phosh 0.56 never sets allow_volume_above_100_percent
desktop.general: When a setting has no effect, check that the code reads it: a field can be declared and tested but never assigned.
desktop.instance: phosh 0.56.0 src/settings/audio-settings.c: the field is only declared and read, so the slider stops at 100% whatever org.gnome.desktop.sound says. Patched here (device/phosh/volume-above-100-percent.patch).

desktop.title: phoc raises a black shield on every output transform change
desktop.general: A black flash on each rotation in phoc is deliberate: the modeset shield hides layer-surface rearrangement and fades out in 150 ms. Every output configuration commit sets mode, scale and transform, so 'only the transform changed' must be found by comparing with the previous commit.
desktop.instance: phoc 0.56.0 src/output.c (modeset_shield). Patch skipping it for rotation alone: device/phoc/rotation-without-shield.patch, untested on the phone.

desktop.title: Phosh restores a portrait pre-lock transform on unlock
desktop.general: On phones Phosh forces the lock screen to portrait and restores the transform saved at lock time. A session that starts locked saves portrait, so anything that rotates the panel during the lock screen is undone at unlock.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: keyboard out at login, lock screen landscape, shell portrait after unlocking. Patch: leave the transform alone when orientation is locked (device/phosh/lockscreen-keep-locked-orientation.patch), untested.

desktop.title: Phosh saves no display configuration
desktop.general: Phosh applies a scale chosen in Settings but writes it nowhere; each login starts from phoc's ini. Persist display settings in phoc.ini.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: scale back to 2 at every login. Default now 1.75 in /etc/phoc.ini; the session uses ~/.config/phoc/phoc.ini when present.

desktop.title: GSettings overrides for other packages' schemas belong in the system profile
desktop.general: An override compiled into one package's schema directory only reaches that package's schemas. For keys of gsettings-desktop-schemas, put the override in a package in the system profile: Guix's glib-schemas profile hook compiles all of them together.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: org.gnome.desktop.sound allow-volume-above-100-percent via pro1x-gsettings-defaults; checked with GSETTINGS_BACKEND=memory gsettings against the phone's compiled schemas: true.

desktop.title: tuigreet remembers nothing without /var/cache/tuigreet
desktop.general: tuigreet's --remember flags write to /var/cache/tuigreet; a Guix system has no /var/cache by default. Create it at activation, owned by the greeter user.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: no /var/cache at all; greeter uid 986.
desktop.source: ls on the phone; commit d6257e1

desktop.title: Phosh does not detect idleness: gnome-session does
desktop.general: Phosh blanks and locks on idle only when gnome-session reports idle through its presence interface (it watches org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay). Without gnome-session, Phosh never blanks or locks by itself. org.gnome.ScreenSaver.SetActive(true) from an idle daemon (swayidle) blanks and starts Phosh's lock-delay timer.
desktop.instance: phosh 0.56 src/screen-saver-manager.c (comment and screen_saver_set_active). pro1x-idle calls SetActive after idle-delay; author confirmed blank and lock.

desktop.title: PulseAudio autospawn can take pipewire-pulse's socket
desktop.general: With PulseAudio's libpulse and binary installed, a client starting before pipewire-pulse listens (or one left from the previous session when pipewire-pulse stops) runs `pulseaudio --start`, which takes the PulseAudio socket; pipewire-pulse then dies and PulseAudio drives the card without the session's UCM settings. Set autospawn = no in /etc/pulse/client.conf and PULSE_CLIENTCONFIG in the session environment (as Guix's pulseaudio-service-type does).
desktop.instance: Pro1X: login with no sound, card named alsa_card.0 with generic profiles, pipewire-pulse defunct ('Address already in use'), pulseaudio started 15 s before PipeWire.
desktop.source: commit 32946bc; ps and session log on the phone

desktop.title: A UCM verb's exec runs during PipeWire's profile probe too
desktop.general: UCM EnableSequence exec commands run whenever the verb is set, including PipeWire's probe of every profile at session start. A helper started from a verb must be single-instance and must not act unless its condition (a call) holds; otherwise copies pile up across logins and their side effects (keep-alive streams, profile holds) run outside calls. Put the card back on the default profile after a call, or WirePlumber saves the call profile and restores it at every login.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: three pro1x-voice-call copies from three logins, keep-alive streams running, card restored to Voice Call (Earpiece) at login; probable cause of the login pops (not yet confirmed by ear).
desktop.source: commit 7aff1ef; ps and WirePlumber state on the phone

desktop.title: callaudiod's speaker switch does nothing with PipeWire 1.2+ per-output profiles
desktop.general: callaudiod 0.1.9 switches sink ports, but PipeWire creates one card profile per output when outputs share a PCM (ConflictingDevice in UCM changes nothing). callaudiod upstream is deprecated; speaker switching in calls is open upstream (pipewire issue 4868). Following callaudiod's state with profile switches changes the profile but not necessarily the DSP voice route.
desktop.instance: Pro1X: profile switched to Voice Call (Mic, Speaker) and back on the button, capture route off on mute, but no audible change (author). Two attempts, stopped.

desktop.title: Phosh's notification banners show no action buttons
desktop.general: Do not rely on notification actions (notify-send -A --wait) for a confirmation in Phosh: banners showed none, and notify-send returned at once without an answer. Use a launcher (with desktop actions for alternatives) and repeated reminders instead.
desktop.instance: Pro1X, phosh 0.56: MMS confirmation redesigned as a Fetch MMS launcher plus 30-min reminders.

desktop.title: Packages missing from the profile: callaudiod, mmsd-tng, stevia, xdg-user-dirs
desktop.general: On a Phosh system without gnome-session, check what gnome-session or a distribution would start or install: callaudiod (Calls' audio routing), mmsd-tng (Chatty's MMS), the OSK (sm.puri.OSK0), xdg-user-dirs-update (Snapshot needs XDG_PICTURES_DIR), gsd-rfkill (Bluetooth state in Phosh and GNOME Settings, with /dev/rfkill writable without logind).
desktop.instance: Pro1X 2026-10-30: each found missing from a user-visible symptom; mmsd-tng and stevia packaged here.

desktop.title: A GSettings override in the system profile does not reach programs whose wrapper puts their own schemas first
desktop.general: Guix's glib-or-gtk wrappers prepend each package's share to XDG_DATA_DIRS. GSettings takes a schema from the first directory whose gschemas.compiled has it, so an override compiled into the system profile is ignored by a program that ships that schema itself (or whose wrapper lists gsettings-desktop-schemas first). Put the override into that package's own schema directory, and run glib-compile-schemas there in your phase: the build system had already compiled the schemas before an add-after 'install phase. Check with gsettings in the program's own environment (copy XDG_DATA_DIRS and XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP from /proc/PID/environ), not a login shell's.
desktop.instance: stevia 0.56.0 (on-screen keyboard) read mobi.phosh.osk ignore-hw-keyboards false although the system profile's override said true; true after the override and glib-compile-schemas went into stevia's own share/glib-2.0/schemas (generation 40, 2026-10-30).
desktop.source: commits 4a17fa5, f083a22, 223a2fa; gsettings with GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR on the stevia package

desktop.title: Desktop-specific GSettings overrides ([schema:Phosh]) beat plain ones in that desktop
desktop.general: glib-compile-schemas supports [schema:DESKTOP] sections that apply when XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP contains DESKTOP, ahead of the plain [schema] section whatever the file order. A shell that ships such overrides (Phosh's 00_mobi.Phosh.gschema.override) wins over a distribution default written without the suffix; write both sections.
desktop.instance: Phosh 0.56 sets [org.gnome.desktop.session:Phosh] idle-delay=60; our idle-delay=180 applied in Sway but Phosh kept blanking at 60 s until the override also wrote the :Phosh section (generation 40: swayidle blanks at 180).
desktop.source: commit 59ad954; schema test compiled with both overrides, XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Phosh

desktop.title: GTK 3 on Guix finds its input-method modules only through GUIX_GTK3_IM_MODULE_FILE
desktop.general: Guix's gtk+ reads the IM module cache from GUIX_GTK3_IM_MODULE_FILE and has no cache in its own output; the variable comes from gtk+'s search path, which is only set when gtk+ itself is in the profile. Without it GTK 3 text fields never use the Wayland IM module, and on-screen keyboards are never asked for. Set it for the session (session-environment-service-type) to the profile's lib/gtk-3.0/3.0.0/immodules-gtk3.cache.
desktop.instance: Phosh session on the Pro1x, generation 36+: no OSK for GTK 3 fields before; /etc/environment now sets it.
desktop.source: commit d6641f0; strings of libgtk-3.so (GUIX_GTK3_IM_MODULE_FILE); stevia debug log
